subject: confounding with sex-specific survival in openCR model

messages.author: 55d961293add928a
messages.subject: confounding with sex-specific survival in openCR model
parts:
Hi everyone, 

I am running an analysis to estimate population growth rate and sex-specific survival to compare the results to estimates derived from a telemetry study of the same population that occurred contemporaneously. Having played around with a lot of variations on detection parameters, I would ideally like to run a JSSAsecrlCL model with sex as a covariate on sigma and phi and a normal movement model, but the variance calculations fail and the error message says confounding likely. When I keep phi constant between sexes, I don't run into any problems. Interestingly, when I run a non-spatial model (p ~ Sex, phi ~ Sex), at least one parameter is not identifiable, but when I run a JSSAsecrlCL model with static movement and sex-specific survival, everything looks good. I have two questions. 1) Is there anything else I can do to try to fit the model with sex-specific survival and activity center movement between sessions (see below for more details)? 2) I know that using static activity centers overestimates sigma and underestimates density, but is there any reason why it would also bias estimates of lambda and phi? Since those are the parameters of interest, should I care about the movement model? The results I get from the static model seem credible.

The dataset isn't great: 269 observations of 54 individuals across 5 sessions. The data come from camera-trap surveys of leopards that occurred in 2005, 2007, 2009, 2011, and 2012. The 2011 survey occurred in a different season and produced very different capture results compared to the other four years. I've attached a simplified script. In addition to the models shown in the script, I played around with starting values, seasonal effects on the fourth session,  kernel radius, and including a finite mixture on move.a, but it hasn't fixed the variance calculations. The kernel radius (20 km) may seem large but has proven necessary for other similar datasets I've been working with. 

If anyone does want to take a look at the data, I've posted an rdata file to google drive that includes the captures data frame ("captures"), the capthist object ("Ph.ch"), a mask object ("msk"), a non-spatial model ("CRmod"), an openCR_list of four spatial models with a "normal" movement model ("openSCR_list"), and a spatial model with a static movement model ("static_mod").

Any suggestions or insights would be greatly appreciated.

Matt Rogan

messages.subject: Re: confounding with sex-specific survival in openCR model
parts: I can't help with the details of model fitting, but simulations in Efford & Schofield 2019 suggest that estimates of population growth rate (lambda) are robust to misspecification of movement (e.g. using a static model when there is actually some movement).
